toc.label: Universal Backdoor Detection (UnivBD)
toc.definition: A post-training method that flags whether a trained classifier is backdoored by finding a target class whose logit margin can be pushed abnormally high by a small common perturbation, without any clean or poisoned training data.
sub_questions: How can you detect a backdoor with no access to training data or triggers?
What single signal reveals every trigger type at once?

toc.label: Backdoor Attack
toc.definition: A training-time attack that makes a classifier behave normally on clean inputs but predict an attacker-chosen target class whenever a specific trigger is present.
sub_questions: What is the attacker's success criterion?

toc.label: Backdoor Trigger
toc.definition: The perturbation (additive noise, a patch, or a blended image) whose presence activates the backdoor.
sub_questions: Why must the trigger be common across inputs?

toc.label: Target Class
toc.definition: The class the attacker wants triggered inputs to be misclassified into.
sub_questions: Why does the target class leave a detectable footprint?

toc.label: Post-Training Defense Scenario
toc.definition: The setting where the defender is handed only a trained classifier — no training set, no clean examples — and must decide if it is backdoored.
sub_questions: What can and cannot the defender assume?

toc.label: Logit Landscape
toc.definition: The classifier's pre-softmax output functions viewed as a surface over input space; a backdoor warps this surface for the target class.
sub_questions: How does a backdoor deform the logits?

toc.label: Maximum Margin (MM) Statistic
toc.definition: The largest achievable gap between a candidate target class logit and the runner-up, over a small common perturbation applied to a batch of inputs.
sub_questions: Why is a backdoored class's margin an outlier?

toc.label: Detection via an Atypical Margin
toc.definition: A class is flagged when its MM statistic is a statistical outlier among all classes.

toc.label: Estimating the Margin by Gradient Ascent
toc.definition: Solving for the common perturbation that maximizes a class's margin using projected gradient ascent on the input.
sub_questions: What constraint keeps the perturbation small?

toc.label: Order-Statistic p-value
toc.definition: A null-model p-value that converts the maximum MM statistic across classes into a calibrated detection decision.
sub_questions: Why use the maximum across classes?

toc.label: Null Distribution of Margins
toc.definition: A distribution fit to the non-outlier classes' MM statistics, giving a reference for what a clean margin looks like.
sub_questions: How is the null fit robustly to outliers?

toc.label: Backdoor Mitigation
toc.definition: Repairing a detected backdoor by bounding neuron activations so the trigger can no longer dominate the logit for the target class.
sub_questions: Can you disable the backdoor without retraining?

toc.label: Bounded-Logit Neuron Clipping
toc.definition: Replacing each neuron's output by a clipped version whose upper bound is optimized to suppress backdoor activations.
sub_questions: Why clip activations rather than weights?

toc.label: Lagrangian for Mitigation
toc.definition: The constrained objective whose Lagrangian yields the per-neuron activation bounds used for mitigation.
sub_questions: What does the multiplier trade off?

toc.label: Detection Performance
toc.definition: Empirical accuracy and efficiency of UnivBD against state-of-the-art detectors across trigger types and datasets.
